meta.title: Operation of Rotary Vacuum Evaporator in Pharmaceutical Chemistry Laboratory

sections.purpose: To remove organic solvents from reaction mixtures and purified product solutions under reduced pressure and controlled temperature, enabling gentle recovery of thermolabile pharmaceutical compounds.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Chemistry laboratory for solvent removal from organic synthesis reaction workups, concentration of extracts, and recovery of recrystallization solvents.
procedure: Check water bath level — fill with distilled water to the recommended level; set the required temperature (typically 30–40°C for low-boiling solvents; 50–60°C for higher-boiling solvents).
Verify cold water or chilled water supply to the condenser (5–15°C) and confirm it is flowing.
Fill the cold trap with ice water or dry ice/acetone mixture to protect the vacuum pump.
Attach the receiving flask and evaporating flask with Keck clips.
Pour the solution to be evaporated into the evaporating flask (maximum 2/3 volume).
Lower the flask into the water bath.
Set rotation speed to 40–80 RPM and switch on rotation.
Open the vacuum valve slowly — monitor the vacuum gauge, target 50–200 mbar.
Once solvent begins to evaporate visibly into the receiving flask, confirm the system is working correctly.
Periodically empty the receiving flask — drain solvent to a labelled waste container.
Continue until evaporation stops (no more solvent visible dripping into the receiving flask).
To finish: close vacuum valve; bleed air back slowly; stop rotation; raise flask from water bath.
Remove the evaporating flask containing the product residue; transfer to a pre-weighed container.
Record: solvent evaporated, temperature, vacuum, duration, and residue weight in the notebook.
precautions: Use only round-bottom flasks — never flat-bottomed or conical flasks under vacuum.
Always use a cold trap — solvent vapours destroy vacuum pump oil.
Bleed vacuum slowly — rapid pressure change causes bumping and sample loss.
Inspect all glassware for cracks before use — vacuum amplifies failure risk of damaged glass.
Do not exceed 60°C bath temperature for heat-sensitive compounds.
Ensure the cold condenser is functioning before starting — warm condenser allows vapours to reach the pump.
Keep anti-bumping chips in the evaporating flask for foaming solutions.
